claims.purpose: Missionism exists to help design organizations so that the rational self-interest of the contributor, the organization, and the customer or beneficiary can point the same way.
claims.noPermanentEntitlement: Authority and economics should not remain permanently concentrated merely because someone arrived first.
claims.measurableMission: A Missionism organization must publicly state a measurable mission; revenue or market capitalization alone is not a sufficient mission.
claims.contributorPath: People who create enduring value must have a viable path to meaningful ownership of that value.
claims.tripleAlignment: An organizational design is incomplete while the incentives of the contributor, the organization, and the customer or beneficiary diverge.
claims.missionRecursion: Missions may contain child missions and participate in parent missions.
claims.missionAutonomy: A child mission may retain autonomy while contributing to a parent mission.
claims.forkability: Missionism-compatible systems must permit exit and independent continuation; a fork is not automatically the canonical Missionism specification.
claims.surviveFounder: If a better version of Missionism is created, people should be free to use it instead.
claims.voluntaryAdoption: Missionism proposes rules for organizations that voluntarily use the system; it does not claim jurisdiction over every organization or every life.
claims.humansNotVariables: Mission optimization is bounded by non-negotiable human constraints; humans are not optimization variables.

humanConstraints.equalStanding: Every person has equal human standing.
humanConstraints.freedomOfConscience: People may believe, worship, question, speak, disagree, and change their minds, while protecting that freedom for others.
humanConstraints.nonCoercion: Missions may not achieve ends through violence, intimidation, or domination.
humanConstraints.humanDignity: Ideas and missions are challengeable; people retain dignity and must not be made the enemy of the mission.
humanConstraints.reciprocity: The freedoms, dignity, and protections claimed for oneself must also be granted to people one profoundly disagrees with.
